domains.name: vessel
domains.description: Manages vessel traffic, scheduling, berthing operations, and marine movements including VTS coordination, anchorage management, ETA/ETB/ATA/ATD tracking, and vessel documentation. Covers vessel profiles (LOA, DWT, GRT, NRT, IMO number), port calls, berth allocation planning, voyage planning, and stowage plans. SSOT for all vessel-related operational data.

products.name: vessel
products.description: Master registry of all vessels calling at the port, including ownership and management hierarchy. Captures the authoritative vessel profile: IMO number, vessel name, flag state (FK to masterdata), vessel type (FK to masterdata), LOA, beam, draft, DWT, GRT, NRT, TEU capacity, call sign, MMSI number, classification society, P&I club, year built, shipyard, and current operational status. Ownership attributes: registered owner, technical manager, commercial operator (disponent owner), ISM company, ship manager, IMO company numbers, country of domicile, and management role types — tracked as SCD Type 2 for ownership change history. Supports ISPS compliance (CSO identification), PSC inspection records, commercial billing relationships, sanctions screening, and vessel risk profiling. SSOT for all vessel identity, static characteristics, and corporate hierarchy referenced across terminal, cargo, marine, and billing domains.

products.name: owner
products.description: Master record of vessel ownership and management entities. Captures registered owner, technical manager, commercial operator (disponent owner), ISM company, and ship manager details including company name, IMO company number, country of domicile, contact details, and management role type. Tracks ownership changes and management transfers over time. Supports ISPS compliance (CSO identification), PSC inspection records, commercial billing relationships, and sanctions screening. Distinct from the customer domain which tracks port community participants as commercial clients — this product captures the vessel's corporate hierarchy as declared in IMO records.

products.name: call
products.description: Core transactional record representing a single vessel visit to the port, from pre-arrival notification through departure. Captures: voyage number, POL, POD, ETA/ETB/ETD, ATA/ATB/ATD, call purpose (loading, discharge, bunkering, transit, lay-up, crew change), cargo type, total TEU/FEU declared, call status, VTS clearance reference. Agent appointment attributes: appointed agent company, agency type (general, husbanding, cargo, protective), appointment scope (single call, voyage series, annual), appointment dates, primary contact, and appointment status. Milestone timestamps: pilot boarded, first line, all fast, gangway down, cargo ops start/end, last line, pilot off. The primary operational anchor entity linking vessel movements to berth allocation, cargo operations, pilotage, towage, and billing. Supports SLA measurement, port call performance reporting (UNCTAD indicators), and agent coordination for document submission authority and billing address routing.
products.reference: Port Call Notification / VTMS Port Call Record

attributes.name: coparn_received_flag

attributes.name: draft_forward_meters

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the movement from start to completion, measured in minutes. Used for operational efficiency analysis and billing calculations.

products.name: call_schedule
products.description: Forward-looking schedule and service route record representing planned port calls for a vessel over a service rotation or voyage series. Service route attributes: service code, service name, operating shipping line(s), alliance designation, rotation of ports in sequence, service frequency (weekly, bi-weekly), vessel string size, average TEU capacity, service type (mainline, feeder, regional), and service status. Schedule attributes: rotation sequence number, planned ETA, planned ETD, planned berth window, cargo volume forecast (TEU), schedule version, schedule source (shipping line EDI, agent submission, VTS pre-notification), and schedule status (provisional, confirmed, amended, cancelled). Supports berth planning horizon management, resource pre-allocation, volume forecasting, and commercial service agreement management. Distinct from call which is the actual operational record of a realized port visit.

attributes.name: port_call_id
attributes.description: Reference to the port call during which this draft survey was conducted. Links the survey to the vessel's visit.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Vessel Planning

attributes.name: primary_draft_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system user who created this draft survey record. Audit trail for accountability.

attributes.name: vessel_id
attributes.description: Reference to the vessel on which the draft survey was performed.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) Ship Identification Number Scheme

attributes.name: aft_draft_port_meters
attributes.description: Draft reading at the aft perpendicular on the port side of the vessel, measured in meters from the waterline to the keel.

attributes.name: aft_draft_starboard_meters
attributes.description: Draft reading at the aft perpendicular on the starboard side of the vessel, measured in meters from the waterline to the keel.

attributes.name: ballast_water_mt
attributes.description: Weight of ballast water on board the vessel at the time of survey, measured in metric tons. Deducted from displacement to calculate cargo weight.
attributes.references: International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships' Ballast Water and Sediments

attributes.name: bol_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the Bill of Lading associated with the cargo being surveyed. Links the draft survey to the cargo documentation.
attributes.references: International Chamber of Commerce - Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600)

attributes.name: bunker_fuel_mt
attributes.description: Weight of bunker fuel oil on board the vessel at the time of survey, measured in metric tons. Deducted from displacement to calculate cargo weight.

attributes.name: calculated_cargo_weight_mt
attributes.description: Net weight of cargo loaded or discharged, calculated by subtracting lightship weight, constant, bunkers, water, ballast, and stores from the displacement. Measured in metric tons. This is the principal quantitative result of the draft survey.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: cargo_type
attributes.description: Type or description of cargo being surveyed (e.g., iron ore, coal, grain, steel coils). Provides context for the survey and weight verification.

attributes.name: certificate_issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the draft survey certificate was officially issued by the surveyor.

attributes.name: certificate_issued_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal draft survey certificate has been issued for this survey. True if certificate issued, False otherwise.

attributes.name: constant_mt
attributes.description: Constant correction factor representing the difference between the actual lightship weight and the documented lightship weight, measured in metric tons. Accounts for permanent additions or removals since last lightship survey.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this draft survey record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: displacement_mt
attributes.description: Total weight of water displaced by the vessel at the surveyed draft, measured in metric tons. Derived from hydrostatic tables and draft readings.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: dwa_allowance_mm
attributes.description: Dock water allowance correction applied when the vessel is in water of intermediate density between salt and fresh water, measured in millimeters.

attributes.name: forward_draft_port_meters
attributes.description: Draft reading at the forward perpendicular on the port side of the vessel, measured in meters from the waterline to the keel.

attributes.name: forward_draft_starboard_meters
attributes.description: Draft reading at the forward perpendicular on the starboard side of the vessel, measured in meters from the waterline to the keel.

attributes.name: fresh_water_mt
attributes.description: Weight of fresh water on board the vessel at the time of survey, measured in metric tons. Deducted from displacement to calculate cargo weight.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: fwa_allowance_mm
attributes.description: Fresh water allowance correction applied when the vessel is in fresh water or dock water, measured in millimeters. Accounts for the difference in buoyancy between salt and fresh water.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this draft survey record was last updated in the system. Audit trail for record modifications.

attributes.name: lightship_weight_mt
attributes.description: Weight of the vessel in light condition (empty, without cargo, fuel, water, stores), measured in metric tons. Used as baseline for cargo weight calculation.

attributes.name: list_degrees
attributes.description: Transverse inclination of the vessel measured in degrees. Positive value indicates list to starboard, negative indicates list to port.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: mean_aft_draft_meters
attributes.description: Average of port and starboard aft draft readings, used in displacement calculations.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: mean_draft_meters
attributes.description: Overall mean draft of the vessel calculated from forward, midship, and aft draft readings, used as the primary input for displacement calculation.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: mean_forward_draft_meters
attributes.description: Average of port and starboard forward draft readings, used in displacement calculations.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: mean_midship_draft_meters
attributes.description: Average of port and starboard midship draft readings, used in displacement calculations.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: midship_draft_port_meters
attributes.description: Draft reading at the midship section on the port side of the vessel, measured in meters from the waterline to the keel.

attributes.name: midship_draft_starboard_meters
attributes.description: Draft reading at the midship section on the starboard side of the vessel, measured in meters from the waterline to the keel.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional notes, observations, or comments recorded by the surveyor regarding the draft survey, including any anomalies, special conditions, or clarifications.

attributes.name: sea_state_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing sea state conditions during the survey (e.g., Douglas Sea Scale 0-9). Affects survey accuracy and reliability.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO) - Sea State Code

attributes.name: stores_provisions_mt
attributes.description: Weight of stores, provisions, and consumables on board the vessel at the time of survey, measured in metric tons. Deducted from displacement to calculate cargo weight.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: survey_accuracy_rating
attributes.description: Surveyor's assessment of the accuracy and reliability of the draft survey results based on conditions and measurement quality: excellent, good, fair, or poor.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Quality Standards

attributes.name: survey_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the draft survey was conducted. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

attributes.name: survey_purpose
attributes.description: Business purpose for conducting the draft survey: cargo weight verification, load line compliance check, demurrage calculation support, charter party contractual requirement, customs declaration, or insurance claim documentation.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Cargo Handling Standards

attributes.name: survey_reference_number
attributes.description: External reference number or certificate number assigned by the surveyor or survey company for this draft survey.

attributes.name: survey_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the draft survey: draft (in progress), completed (survey finished), certified (certificate issued), disputed (under dispute), or cancelled.

attributes.name: survey_type
attributes.description: Type of draft survey conducted: initial (before loading), final (after loading/discharge), intermediate (during operations), pre-loading, or post-discharge.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: surveyor_company_name
attributes.description: Name of the marine surveyor company or independent surveyor who conducted the draft survey.

attributes.name: surveyor_license_number
attributes.description: Professional license or certification number of the surveyor who conducted the survey.
attributes.references: National Maritime Safety Authority - Surveyor Certification

attributes.name: surveyor_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual surveyor who performed the draft survey measurements and calculations.

attributes.name: trim_meters
attributes.description: Difference between forward and aft drafts. Positive value indicates trim by stern (aft deeper), negative indicates trim by bow (forward deeper).
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

attributes.name: water_density_kg_per_m3
attributes.business_glossary_term: Water Density (Kilograms per Cubic Meter - kg/m³)
attributes.description: Density of the water in which the vessel is floating at the time of survey, measured in kilograms per cubic meter. Used for displacement corrections.
attributes.references: International Association of Marine Surveyors - Draft Survey Standards

tag_set.value: Water Density (Kilograms per Cubic Meter - kg/m³)

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Description of weather conditions at the time of the survey (e.g., calm, moderate wind, rough seas). Weather can affect draft reading accuracy.

products.name: service_route
products.description: Master record of a shipping line's scheduled service route (liner service) calling at the port. Captures service code, service name, operating shipping line(s), alliance service designation, rotation of ports in sequence, service frequency (weekly, bi-weekly), vessel string size (number of vessels deployed), average vessel TEU capacity, service type (mainline, feeder, regional), and service status (active, suspended, discontinued). Supports berth window planning, volume forecasting, and commercial service agreement management.
products.reference: Liner Service Route / Shipping Line Service String

attributes.name: service_route_id
attributes.description: Primary key for service_route

attributes.name: preferred_berth_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the preferred or contracted berth for this service. Used in berth allocation planning and service level agreement management.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Berth Allocation Standards

attributes.name: service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.agreement. Business justification: Service routes are governed by berth allocation agreements and service contracts with shipping lines/alliances. Required for commercial planning, berth allocation priority, rate schedule application,

attributes.name: shipping_line_id
attributes.description: add column shipping_line_id (BIGINT) with FK to masterdata.shipping_line.shipping_line_id - service routes are operated by shipping lines and must reference the operator

attributes.name: alliance_name
attributes.description: Name of the shipping alliance or consortium operating the service (e.g., 2M Alliance, THE Alliance, Ocean Alliance). Null if service is operated by a single carrier outside alliance framework.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Alliance Service Standards

attributes.name: alliance_service_designation
attributes.description: Alliance-level service identifier or designation code used when multiple carriers jointly operate the service under a shared service agreement.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Alliance Service Standards

attributes.name: average_vessel_beam_meters
attributes.description: Average beam (width) in meters of vessels deployed on this service. Used for berth compatibility assessment and safe navigation planning.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) - Vessel Dimension Standards

attributes.name: average_vessel_capacity_teu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Vessel Capacity Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU)
attributes.description: Average nominal container capacity in TEU of vessels deployed on this service. Used for volume forecasting, berth capacity planning, and yard space allocation. TEU is the standard unit for measuring container vessel capacity.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - TEU Measurement Standards

tag_set.value: Average Vessel Capacity Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU)

attributes.name: average_vessel_draft_meters
attributes.description: Average maximum draft in meters of vessels deployed on this service. Critical for ensuring channel depth and berth depth compatibility, and for tide-dependent berthing planning.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) - Vessel Dimension Standards

attributes.name: average_vessel_loa_meters
attributes.description: Average length overall in meters of vessels deployed on this service. LOA is critical for berth allocation planning and ensuring adequate berth length availability.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) - Vessel Dimension Standards

attributes.name: dangerous_cargo_percentage
attributes.description: Expected percentage of container volume classified as dangerous goods under IMDG Code. Used for safety planning, segregation requirements, and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) - International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code

attributes.name: edi_service_code
attributes.description: Service code used in EDI messages (BAPLIE, COPARN, IFTMIN) for electronic data exchange with shipping lines and port community systems. Ensures consistent service identification across systems.
attributes.references: United Nations Centre for Trade Facilitation and Electronic Business (UN/CEFACT) - EDI Standards

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this service configuration becomes effective. Used for managing service changes, new service launches, and historical tracking.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date until which this service configuration remains effective. Null for currently active services with no planned end date. Used for managing service suspensions, discontinuations, and configuration changes.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: expected_container_volume_teu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Expected Container Volume Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU)
attributes.description: Forecasted or contracted container volume in TEU per vessel call for this service at this port. Used for yard planning, equipment allocation, and commercial performance tracking.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Volume Forecasting Standards

tag_set.value: Expected Container Volume Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU)

attributes.name: export_volume_percentage
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total container volume that is export (loading) cargo. Used for yard planning and gate operation forecasting.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Volume Forecasting Standards

attributes.name: import_volume_percentage
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total container volume that is import (discharge) cargo. Used for yard planning and gate operation forecasting. Complement is export and transshipment volume.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Volume Forecasting Standards

attributes.name: last_call_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent vessel call for this service at this port. Used for service activity monitoring and performance tracking.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Performance Tracking

attributes.name: next_scheduled_call_date
attributes.description: Date of the next scheduled vessel call for this service at this port. Used for near-term berth planning and operational readiness.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Scheduling Standards

attributes.name: operating_shipping_line
attributes.description: Primary shipping line or carrier operating the service. May be a single carrier or lead carrier in a vessel sharing agreement. Used for commercial relationship management and billing.

attributes.name: port_call_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential position of this port within the service rotation (e.g., 1 for first port, 2 for second port). Used for berth window planning and voyage sequencing.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Port Rotation Standards

attributes.name: port_rotation_sequence
attributes.description: Ordered list of ports in the service rotation, typically represented as comma-separated port codes or names (e.g., Singapore-Hong Kong-Shanghai-Busan-Los Angeles-Oakland). Defines the complete loop or string that vessels follow on this service.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Port Rotation Standards

attributes.name: port_stay_duration_hours
attributes.description: Average or planned duration in hours that vessels on this service spend at this port, from berthing to departure. Used for berth window planning and terminal resource allocation.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Berth Planning Standards

attributes.name: record_created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that created this service route record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service route record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_by
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that last modified this service route record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service route record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization.

attributes.name: reefer_percentage
attributes.description: Expected percentage of container volume that requires refrigeration (reefer containers). Used for reefer plug allocation planning and power supply capacity management.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Specialized Cargo Standards

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special handling requirements, operational constraints, or other relevant information about the service that does not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: rotation_duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of days required to complete one full service rotation from first port back to first port. Used to calculate vessel string requirements and service frequency.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Scheduling Standards

attributes.name: service_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the shipping line to identify the liner service (e.g., AE1, FE2, TP3). Industry-standard identifier used in vessel schedules, berth planning, and commercial agreements.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Identification Standards

attributes.name: service_commencement_date
attributes.description: Date when the service first commenced operations at this port. Used for historical analysis and service tenure tracking.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: service_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency of vessel calls at this port for the service. Weekly services provide one call per week; bi-weekly provides two calls per week; fortnightly provides one call every two weeks. Critical for berth planning and volume forecasting.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Scheduling Standards

attributes.name: service_name
attributes.description: Full commercial name of the liner service as marketed by the shipping line (e.g., Asia-Europe Express, Transpacific Loop 3). Used in customer-facing documentation and service agreements.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Identification Standards

attributes.name: service_reliability_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of vessel calls that arrived within the scheduled time window over a measurement period. Key performance indicator for service quality and customer satisfaction.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Level Agreement Standards

attributes.name: service_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the liner service. Active services are currently calling at the port; suspended services are temporarily halted; discontinued services have been permanently terminated; planned services are scheduled to commence in the future.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Classification of the liner service based on operational scope and connectivity. Mainline services connect major hub ports across continents; feeder services connect regional ports to mainline hubs; regional services operate within a geographic region; shuttle services provide point-to-point connectivity; express services offer premium transit times.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Classification Standards

attributes.name: terminal_operator
attributes.description: Name of the terminal operating company handling this service. Used for operational coordination and commercial agreement management.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Terminal Operations Standards

attributes.name: transshipment_volume_percentage
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total container volume that is transshipment cargo (discharged from one vessel and loaded onto another). Critical for hub port operations and inter-terminal transfer planning.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Volume Forecasting Standards

attributes.name: vessel_string_size
attributes.description: Number of vessels deployed on this service rotation. Determines service frequency and capacity. For example, a 7-vessel string on a 49-day rotation provides weekly frequency.
attributes.references: International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) - Service Capacity Planning

products.name: crew_list
products.description: Master record of crew members aboard a vessel during a port call, as declared in the crew list submitted under IMO FAL Form 5. Captures crew member name, nationality, rank/position, passport number, seafarer's book number, STCW certificate reference, date of joining, date of signing off, and crew change type (joining, departing, remaining). Supports ISPS security screening, immigration compliance, crew change coordination, and port health authority notifications. Distinct from the workforce domain which manages port employees.
products.reference: IMO FAL Form 5 Crew List / STCW Convention

attributes.name: crew_list_id
attributes.description: Primary key for crew_list

attributes.name: access_credential_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.access_credential. Business justification: Crew members granted shore leave require temporary access credentials for port facility entry. Immigration and port security issue credentials after ISPS screening, passport verification, and shore le

attributes.name: nationality_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Crew nationality determines visa requirements, shore leave authorization, immigration clearance procedures, and MLC compliance verification. Required for port health clearance, immigration processing,

attributes.name: ohs_incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.ohs_incident. Business justification: Crew members are frequently injured parties in port-side incidents during cargo operations, gangway accidents, or vessel maintenance. Incident reports must identify the specific crew member involved,

attributes.name: port_call_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific port call during which this crew member is aboard the vessel. Links crew list to vessel visit.

attributes.name: vessel_id
attributes.description: Reference to the vessel on which this crew member is serving. Links crew member to vessel master record.

attributes.name: visitor_log_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.visitor_log. Business justification: Crew shore leave is logged as visitor access when entering restricted port areas beyond the vessel berth. Security posts record crew entry/exit timestamps, zones accessed, and escort requirements. Vis

attributes.name: contact_address
attributes.description: Shore-based contact address for the crew member. Used for emergency contact and repatriation purposes.

attributes.name: contact_phone_number
attributes.description: Shore-based contact phone number for the crew member or their next of kin. Used for emergency notifications.

attributes.name: crew_change_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member is joining the vessel, departing (signing off), remaining aboard, or in transit through the port. Critical for immigration and crew change coordination.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Form 5, Port State Control

attributes.name: crew_list_status
attributes.description: Current status of the crew member on this vessel port call. Tracks lifecycle from active service through sign-off or other separation events.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Convention, ILO Maritime Labour Convention

attributes.name: crew_member_family_name
attributes.description: Family name (surname) of the crew member as it appears on their passport or seafarer identity document. Required for immigration and security screening.

attributes.name: crew_member_given_name
attributes.description: Given name (first name) of the crew member as it appears on their passport or seafarer identity document. Required for immigration and security screening.

attributes.name: crew_member_middle_name
attributes.description: Middle name or patronymic of the crew member if applicable. Optional field for complete name identification.

attributes.name: date_of_birth
attributes.description: Crew member's date of birth as recorded on their passport or seafarer identity document. Used for identity verification and age-related compliance.

attributes.name: date_of_joining_vessel
attributes.description: Date on which the crew member joined the vessel. Marks the start of their current tour of duty and is used to calculate sea service time.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Form 5, ILO Maritime Labour Convention

attributes.name: expected_date_of_signing_off
attributes.description: Anticipated date on which the crew member will sign off the vessel and complete their tour of duty. Used for crew change planning and relief scheduling.

attributes.name: expected_port_of_signing_off
attributes.description: Name of the port where the crew member is expected to sign off the vessel. Used for crew change coordination and travel arrangements.

attributes.name: isps_screening_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Screening Timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when ISPS security screening was completed for the crew member. Used for audit trail and compliance verification.
attributes.references: ISPS Code Part A and B

tag_set.value: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Screening Timestamp

attributes.name: isps_security_screening_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Security Screening Status
attributes.description: Result of ISPS security screening for the crew member. Cleared status is required for vessel operations in ISPS-compliant ports.
attributes.references: ISPS Code Part A and B

tag_set.value: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Security Screening Status

attributes.name: medical_certificate_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the crew member's medical fitness certificate expires. Must be valid for the crew member to serve aboard the vessel.
attributes.references: ILO Maritime Labour Convention 2006 - Standard A1.2

attributes.name: medical_certificate_number
attributes.description: Medical certificate number confirming the crew member is medically fit for sea service. Required under ILO Maritime Labour Convention.
attributes.references: ILO Maritime Labour Convention 2006 - Standard A1.2

attributes.name: next_of_kin_name
attributes.description: Full name of the crew member's next of kin or emergency contact person. Critical for emergency notifications and repatriation.

attributes.name: next_of_kin_phone_number
attributes.description: Contact phone number for the crew member's next of kin. Primary channel for emergency notifications.

attributes.name: next_of_kin_relationship
attributes.description: Relationship of the next of kin to the crew member (e.g., spouse, parent, sibling). Used for emergency contact prioritization.

attributes.name: passport_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the crew member's passport expires. Must be valid for the duration of the port call and voyage to meet immigration requirements.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Form 5, Port State Control

attributes.name: passport_issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the crew member's passport was issued. Used to verify document validity and authenticity.

attributes.name: passport_issuing_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code of the country that issued the crew member's passport. May differ from nationality in some cases.

attributes.name: passport_number
attributes.description: Passport number of the crew member. Primary travel document identifier for immigration clearance and port state control inspections.

attributes.name: place_of_birth
attributes.description: City and country where the crew member was born. May be required by certain port state authorities for immigration processing.

attributes.name: port_health_clearance_status
attributes.description: Health clearance status assigned by port health authority. Cleared status is required before crew can disembark or vessel can commence cargo operations.
attributes.references: IHR 2005 (International Health Regulations), IMO FAL Convention

attributes.name: port_of_joining
attributes.description: Name of the port where the crew member joined the vessel. Used for crew change tracking and repatriation planning.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Form 5, ILO Maritime Labour Convention

attributes.name: rank_position
attributes.description: The crew member's rank or position aboard the vessel as per the ship's crew list. Determines responsibilities and STCW certification requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: master|chief_officer|second_officer|third_officer|chief_engineer|second_engineer|third_engineer|bosun|able_seaman|ordinary_seaman|deck_cadet|engine_cadet|radio_officer|electrician|fitter|oiler|wiper|cook|steward|messman|pumpman|other — 22 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: STCW Convention, ILO Maritime Labour Convention

attributes.name: record_created_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that created this crew list record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this crew list record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: record_updated_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified this crew list record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this crew list record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes or special circumstances related to the crew member's status, documentation, or port call requirements.

attributes.name: seafarers_book_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the seafarer's book expires. Must be valid for the crew member to serve aboard the vessel.

attributes.name: seafarers_book_issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the seafarer's book was issued. Used to verify document validity and seafaring experience.

attributes.name: seafarers_book_number
attributes.description: Seafarer's discharge book or continuous discharge certificate number. Official record of sea service and qualifications issued by flag state.
attributes.references: ILO Maritime Labour Convention 2006, STCW Convention

attributes.name: shore_leave_authorized_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member has been authorized for shore leave by port immigration authorities. True if authorized, false if restricted to vessel.

attributes.name: stcw_certificate_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) Certificate Expiry Date
attributes.description: Date on which the STCW certificate expires. Crew member must hold valid certification to serve in their assigned rank.
attributes.references: STCW Convention 1978 as amended, Port State Control

tag_set.value: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) Certificate Expiry Date

attributes.name: stcw_certificate_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) Certificate Grade
attributes.description: Grade or level of the STCW certificate held by the crew member (e.g., Master Unlimited, Chief Engineer, Officer of the Watch). Determines authorized duties.

tag_set.value: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) Certificate Grade

attributes.name: stcw_certificate_issue_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) Certificate Issue Date
attributes.description: Date on which the STCW certificate was issued. Used to verify currency of qualifications.

products.name: deployment
products.description: This association product represents the operational deployment of a stevedore gang to a specific vessel port call. It captures the assignment of labour resources to cargo operations, tracking scheduled and actual work times, productivity metrics, and operational outcomes. Each record links one gang to one call with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific deployment event.. Existence Justification: In maritime terminal operations, a single vessel port call requires multiple stevedore gangs deployed across different hatches, shifts, and cargo operation types (loading, discharge, restow, lashing). Conversely, each gang is deployed to multiple vessel calls throughout their operational roster period. Gang deployment is a core operational business process actively managed by terminal planners, with rich transactional data including scheduled and actual times, productivity metrics (moves per hour), stoppage tracking, hatch assignments, and payroll integration.

attributes.description: The type of cargo handled by this gang during this deployment. Determines handling requirements, safety protocols, and productivity targets.

attributes.name: deployment_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this gang deployment was created or assigned in the system. Used for audit and planning history.

attributes.name: gang_size_actual

attributes.name: moves_completed

attributes.name: moves_per_hour

attributes.name: operation_type

attributes.name: teu_handled

products.name: agency_appointment
products.description: This association product represents the Agency Appointment contract between a vessel and a port community participant acting as the vessel's agent. It captures the formal appointment of a port agent (shipping agent, husbandry agent, protective agent, or customs broker) to represent and provide services to a vessel during port calls. Each record links one vessel to one port community participant with appointment-specific attributes including agency type, scope of authority, appointment period, commission structure, and service fee arrangements that exist only in the context of this agency relationship.. Existence Justification: Vessel agency appointments are genuine operational M:N relationships in maritime logistics. A single vessel requires multiple agents across different ports and service types (husbandry agent in Singapore, protective agent in Rotterdam, customs broker in Los Angeles), and a single port agent company services multiple vessels simultaneously. The business actively manages these appointments as formal contracts with specific scope, authority levels, commission rates, and appointment periods.

attributes.name: agency_appointment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each vessel agency appointment record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: port_community_participant_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Vessel Agency Appointment - Port Community Participant Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the port community participant acting as the vessel agent

tag_set.value: Vessel Agency Appointment - Port Community Participant Id

attributes.name: vessel_call_id
attributes.description: add column vessel_call_id (BIGINT) with FK to vessel.call.call_id - agency appointments are made in context of a specific vessel call

attributes.name: vessel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vessel being represented by the appointed agent

attributes.name: agency_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of agency service being provided. Husbandry agents handle operational services (pilotage, tugs, linesmen, provisions), protective agents represent cargo interests, customs brokers handle customs clearance, liner agents represent shipping lines on a standing basis, and port agents provide general port services.

attributes.name: appointing_party_imo_company_number
attributes.description: IMO company identification number of the entity that made the agency appointment. Links to the vessel ownership/management hierarchy.

attributes.name: appointing_party_name
attributes.description: Name of the entity that made the agency appointment (typically the vessel owner, technical manager, or commercial operator). Identifies who has the authority to appoint and terminate the agent.

attributes.name: appointment_created_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who created the agency appointment record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: appointment_created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when the agency appointment record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and appointment history tracking.

attributes.name: appointment_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the agency appointment expires or is scheduled to terminate. May be null for open-ended appointments that continue until explicitly terminated.

attributes.name: appointment_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique business reference number assigned to the agency appointment. Used in commercial correspondence, invoicing, and port authority documentation.

attributes.name: appointment_scope
attributes.description: Textual description of the scope of authority and services covered by the agency appointment. Defines what the agent is authorized to do on behalf of the vessel (e.g., 'Full husbandry services including berth booking, pilotage arrangement, crew changes, and bunker coordination' or 'Customs clearance only').

attributes.name: appointment_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the agency appointment becomes effective. The agent is authorized to act on behalf of the vessel from this date forward.

attributes.name: appointment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the agency appointment. Active indicates the appointment is in force, Suspended indicates temporary hold, Terminated indicates early cancellation, Expired indicates natural end of appointment period.

attributes.name: authority_level
attributes.description: Level of decision-making authority granted to the agent. Full authority allows agent to commit vessel to services and expenses up to approved limits, limited authority requires pre-approval for major items, notification only means agent coordinates but does not commit.

attributes.name: commission_rate_percent
attributes.description: Percentage commission rate paid to the agent on port service charges arranged on behalf of the vessel. Typically ranges from 2.5% to 7.5% depending on service type and volume. Commercially sensitive data.

attributes.name: financial_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum amount the agent is authorized to commit on behalf of the vessel without seeking additional approval. Null indicates no specific limit or full authority level does not require limits.

attributes.name: financial_limit_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the financial limit amount.

attributes.name: port_of_appointment
attributes.description: UN/LOCODE of the port where this agency appointment is valid. Many vessels have different agents at different ports. Null indicates the appointment is valid at all ports.

attributes.name: service_fee_structure
attributes.description: Billing model for the agency services. Commission-only means agent earns percentage of arranged services, flat fee means fixed amount per call, commission plus fee combines both, time and materials means hourly billing. Commercially sensitive data.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Reason for early termination of the agency appointment if status is Terminated. Examples include poor service performance, change of vessel ownership, vessel sold, or commercial dispute. Null if appointment is active or expired naturally.

products.name: service_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the contractual service relationship between a vessel and a vendor. It captures the specific services provided by vendors to vessels, including service type, contract terms, validity periods, and performance tracking. Each record links one vessel to one vendor with attributes that exist only in the context of this service relationship. Supports procurement planning, vendor performance management, and vessel operational readiness tracking.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, vessels require multiple specialized vendors across different service categories (ship agents, chandlers, waste contractors, bunker suppliers, repair yards, crew services) at different ports and operational contexts. Each vendor serves multiple vessels across different shipping lines and vessel types. The business actively manages these service relationships as 'Vessel Service Agreements' with specific contract terms, validity periods, service types, and performance ratings that are unique to each vessel-vendor pairing.

attributes.name: service_agreement_id

attributes.name: performance_rating
attributes.description: Performance rating for this specific vendor-vessel service relationship, typically on a scale of 0.00 to 5.00. Captures service quality, timeliness, compliance, and responsiveness specific to this vessel-vendor pairing. Used for vendor selection and contract renewal decisions.

attributes.name: preferred_vendor_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this vendor is designated as a preferred supplier for this service type for this specific vessel. Used for procurement routing and vendor selection workflows.

attributes.name: service_type

attributes.name: valid_to_date

products.name: charter
products.description: This association product represents the charter contract between a vessel and a shipping line. It captures the commercial and operational relationship where a shipping line operates a vessel under various charter arrangements (time charter, voyage charter, bareboat charter). Each record links one vessel to one shipping line with charter-specific attributes including charter type, duration, and operational responsibility flags. This is the operational SSOT for vessel-carrier relationships used in vessel scheduling, commercial billing, fleet management, and regulatory reporting.. Existence Justification: In maritime operations, vessels operate under complex charter arrangements where a single vessel can simultaneously have relationships with multiple shipping lines in different operational capacities (owner, bareboat charterer, time charterer, slot charterer). Conversely, shipping lines operate fleets of multiple vessels under various charter types. Charter agreements are actively managed business contracts with specific attributes (charter type, duration, operational responsibility splits) that belong to neither the vessel nor the shipping line alone, but to the relationship itself.

attributes.name: charter_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for this vessel charter agreement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: port_community_participant_id
attributes.description: add column port_community_participant_id (BIGINT) with FK to customer.port_community_participant.port_community_participant_id - charters involve a charterer party who is a port community participant

attributes.name: shipping_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the shipping line master record. Identifies which carrier is operating the vessel under this charter.

attributes.name: vessel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vessel master record. Identifies which vessel is subject to this charter agreement.

attributes.name: bareboat_charter_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a bareboat (demise) charter where the charterer takes full possession and operational control of the vessel, effectively operating it as if they were the owner.

attributes.name: charter_type
attributes.description: Type of charter arrangement governing this vessel-carrier relationship. TIME_CHARTER: carrier hires vessel for specified period; VOYAGE_CHARTER: carrier hires vessel for specific voyage; BAREBOAT_CHARTER: carrier takes full operational control; SLOT_CHARTER: carrier leases container slots; DEMISE_CHARTER: full transfer of possession and control.

attributes.name: commercial_operator_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this shipping line is the commercial operator (disponent owner) of the vessel under this charter, responsible for commercial decisions, cargo booking, and freight revenue.

attributes.name: commercial_operator_imo_company_number
attributes.description: Unique IMO company identification number assigned to the commercial operator organization. [Moved from vessel: This is relationship-specific data that varies by charter arrangement. The commercial operator IMO number should be derived from the shipping_line master record linked through this association, not stored redundantly in the vessel record.]

attributes.name: commercial_operator_name
attributes.description: Name of the entity commercially operating the vessel under charter or management agreement. The disponent owner controls cargo bookings and voyage planning. [Moved from vessel: This attribute currently exists in the vessel product but represents relationship-specific data. A vessel can have different commercial operators through different charter arrangements simultaneously or over time. This belongs in the vessel_charter association with the commercial_operator_flag to properly model the many-to-many reality of vessel charter relationships.]

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this charter relationship record was first created in the port system.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when this charter agreement expires or was terminated. Null indicates an active ongoing charter with no fixed end date.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this charter agreement. ACTIVE: charter is in effect; SUSPENDED: temporarily inactive; TERMINATED: charter has ended; PENDING: charter signed but not yet commenced.

attributes.name: party_reference
attributes.description: External reference number or identifier for the charter party agreement document governing this vessel-carrier relationship. Used for contract management and legal reference.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when this charter agreement became effective and the shipping line assumed operational responsibility for the vessel under the terms of this charter.

attributes.name: technical_manager_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this shipping line is responsible for technical management of the vessel under this charter, including maintenance, crew management, and technical operations.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this charter relationship record was last modified.

products.name: port_call
products.description: This association product represents the operational event of a vessel calling at a specific port location. It captures the complete port call lifecycle including arrival, berthing, operations, and departure. Each record links one vessel to one port location with attributes that track call-specific operational data, performance metrics, and access control decisions. This is the foundational operational record for terminal operations, marine services billing, and vessel performance analytics.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, vessels make multiple calls at multiple port locations throughout their operational life, and each port location receives thousands of vessels over time. Each port call is a distinct operational event with its own lifecycle (arrival, berthing, operations, departure), performance metrics, cargo volumes, charges, and access control decisions. Port calls are actively managed by marine operations teams as standalone business events with rich operational data.

attributes.name: port_call_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the port call record. Primary key.

attributes.name: infrastructure_berth_allocation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to the specific berth assignment record if this call involved berthing operations. Links to berth scheduling system.

attributes.name: port_location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the port location where the call occurred

attributes.name: vessel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vessel making the port call

attributes.name: access_restriction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this vessel has access restrictions or blacklist status for this specific port location.

attributes.name: arrival_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when the vessel arrived at the port location (pilot boarding or berth arrival depending on location type).

attributes.name: call_performance_rating
attributes.description: Overall performance rating for this port call based on operational efficiency, safety compliance, and commercial metrics.

attributes.name: call_purpose
attributes.description: Primary business purpose of the port call. Determines operational workflows and billing categories.

attributes.name: call_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of this call for the vessel at this specific port location. Enables tracking of repeat visits (1st call, 2nd call, etc.).

attributes.name: call_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the port call in the lifecycle workflow.

attributes.name: cargo_volume_tonnes
attributes.description: Total cargo volume handled during this port call in metric tonnes. Aggregated from cargo operations.

attributes.name: container_moves_count
attributes.description: Total number of container moves (load + discharge) performed during this port call. Key performance metric for container terminals.

attributes.name: created_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when this port call record was created in the system.

attributes.name: departure_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when the vessel departed from the port location.

attributes.name: last_updated_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when this port call record was last modified.

attributes.name: port_stay_hours
attributes.description: Total duration of the port call in hours, calculated from arrival to departure. Used for performance analytics and berth utilization metrics.

attributes.name: preferred_location_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this port location is a preferred calling point for this vessel based on operational history and performance.

attributes.name: psc_deficiency_count

attributes.name: psc_inspection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Port State Control inspection was conducted during this call.

attributes.name: restriction_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why access restrictions apply to this vessel-location combination (e.g., PSC detention history, commercial dispute, safety incident).

attributes.name: total_port_charges_amount
attributes.description: Total port charges billed for this call including berth dues, pilotage, towage, and other marine services.

products.name: call_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of port workforce personnel to vessel port calls. It captures the specific role, time window, and responsibility area for each employee assigned to support a vessel visit. Each record links one port call to one employee with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship. Supports multi-role tracking, shift handover coordination, and operational accountability for vessel service delivery.. Existence Justification: In port operations, a single vessel call requires multiple employees in different operational roles (port captain, VTS officer, security officer, customs liaison, operations supervisor, pilots, linesmen, stevedore foremen, equipment operators, cargo inspectors) working simultaneously or in sequence across the call lifecycle. Conversely, each employee handles multiple vessel calls per shift, day, or week depending on their role and the port's traffic volume. The business actively manages these assignments with role-specific responsibilities, time windows, shift types, and responsibility areas.

attributes.description: The specific operational role the employee is performing for this port call. Determines responsibilities, authority level, and coordination requirements. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: assignment_start_timestamp

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this assignment. Scheduled indicates planned but not yet active; active indicates employee is currently on duty; completed indicates assignment finished normally; relieved indicates handover to another employee; cancelled indicates assignment was not fulfilled.

attributes.name: shift_type

products.name: call_icd_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the cargo distribution allocation between a vessel port call and an inland container depot. It captures the volume of cargo (in TEU) allocated from a specific port call to a specific ICD facility, along with the service agreement terms, effective dates, and primary cargo type for that allocation. Each record links one port call to one ICD facility with attributes that exist only in the context of this cargo distribution relationship.. Existence Justification: In maritime logistics operations, a single vessel port call distributes cargo to multiple inland container depots based on destination routing, and each ICD facility receives containers from multiple vessel calls throughout its operations. The port manages cargo distribution allocations as operational records with specific volume commitments, effective dates, and service agreements for each port-call-to-ICD relationship.

products.name: call_inspection
products.description: This association product represents the inspection event linking a vessel port call to a safety inspection record. It captures the specific scope, timing, and outcomes when a safety inspection is conducted in the context of a particular port call. Each record links one port call to one safety inspection with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, such as the specific inspection scope for that call, findings relevant to that vessel visit, and follow-up actions required before departure clearance.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, a single port call can undergo multiple safety inspections (PSC, ISPS security check, cargo safety audit, environmental compliance inspection) during the vessel's stay. Conversely, a single safety inspection campaign (e.g., coordinated PSC inspection day) can cover multiple vessels/port calls simultaneously. The business actively manages these inspection-to-call associations, tracking which inspections have been completed for each call, whether findings block departure clearance, and what follow-up actions are required before the vessel can sail.

attributes.name: deficiencies_found

attributes.name: detention_flag

attributes.name: inspection_scope
attributes.description: The specific scope of this inspection as it relates to this particular port call. A single safety inspection may cover multiple calls (e.g., PSC campaign), and this attribute captures what aspects were inspected for THIS call specifically.

attributes.name: inspection_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when this inspection was conducted for this port call. Critical for tracking whether inspection occurred before cargo operations commenced or before departure clearance.

domains.name: terminal
domains.description: Manages container terminal operations including yard management, container stacking, gate operations, equipment dispatch (RTG, STS, ASC, QC, MHC), TOS integration (NAVIS N4, TOPS Expert), CY operations, and container tracking (RFID). Covers TEU/FEU handling, LoLo/RoRo operations, CFS activities, and terminal performance KPIs. SSOT for terminal operational execution.

products.name: yard_block
products.description: Master data for container yard blocks within the terminal. Defines physical layout including block identifier, row/tier/bay configuration, ground slot capacity, maximum stacking height, block type (import, export, transshipment, reefer, dangerous goods, empty), surface type, and operational status. Parent entity for all yard_slot records. SSOT for yard spatial planning and container stacking configuration in NAVIS N4 and TOPS Expert TOS.

attributes.name: yard_block_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the container yard block. Primary key. MASTER_RESOURCE role entity representing physical yard infrastructure for container stacking operations.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Yard Management Module

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Yard blocks function as cost centers for yard operations in terminal accounting. Costs (labor, equipment, utilities) and productivity metrics are tracked by block for operational management, budgeting

attributes.name: port_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.port_asset. Business justification: Yard blocks are infrastructure assets with acquisition costs, depreciation schedules, and maintenance lifecycles. Required for capital asset register, infrastructure valuation, pavement maintenance pl

attributes.name: terminal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent container terminal facility that owns and operates this yard block. Establishes organizational hierarchy for multi-terminal port operations.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Terminal Configuration Module

attributes.name: terminal_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the logical yard zone grouping that this block belongs to. Yard zones aggregate multiple blocks for operational planning, resource allocation, and performance reporting.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Yard Management Module

attributes.name: area_square_meters
attributes.description: Total surface area of the yard block in square meters. Calculated as length_meters × width_meters. Used for density analysis, utilization reporting, and infrastructure planning.
attributes.references: PIANC (World Association for Waterborne Transport Infrastructure) Port Infrastructure Design Standards

attributes.name: bay_count
attributes.description: Number of container bays configured in the yard block layout. Bays run parallel to the equipment travel path and define the block's length dimension. Each bay typically accommodates one 40-foot container (FEU) or two 20-foot containers (TEU).
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Yard Management Module; TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit) and FEU (Forty-foot Equivalent Unit) Standards

attributes.name: block_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code identifying the yard block within the terminal. Used for operational communication, TOS integration, and equipment dispatch instructions.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Yard Management Module

attributes.name: block_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the yard block for operational reference and reporting purposes.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Yard Management Module

attributes.name: block_type
attributes.description: Classification of the yard block based on primary container handling purpose. Determines container allocation rules, equipment requirements, and operational workflows.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System - Yard Management Module; International Association of Ports and Harbors (IAPH) Terminal Design Guidelines

attributes.name: cctv_coverage
attributes.description: Indicates whether the yard block is covered by CCTV surveillance systems for security monitoring, incident investigation, and operational oversight per ISPS Code requirements.

attributes.name: commissioning_date

attributes.name: ground_slot_capacity

attributes.name: imdg_certified

products.name: container_visit
products.description: Transactional record of a container's complete terminal visit lifecycle from arrival (gate-in, vessel discharge, or rail-in) to departure (gate-out, vessel load, or rail-out). Core operational entity linking all terminal activities — gate transactions, equipment moves, reefer monitoring, service orders, and hazmat declarations reference this record. attributes.name: oog_overhang_rear_cm

attributes.name: oog_overhang_right_cm

attributes.name: oog_overheight_cm

attributes.name: plan_approved_timestamp

attributes.name: plan_status

attributes.name: plan_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: plan_version

attributes.name: planned_crane_count

attributes.name: planned_gang_count

attributes.name: planned_operation_end

attributes.name: planned_operation_start

attributes.name: pod_code

attributes.name: pol_code

attributes.name: pre_marshalling_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether containers require pre-marshalling or repositioning in the yard prior to vessel loading to optimize load sequence.

attributes.name: reefer_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the container is a refrigerated unit requiring temperature control and power connection.

attributes.name: reefer_temperature_c
attributes.description: Required temperature setting in Celsius for refrigerated containers. Null for non-reefer units.

attributes.name: resource_allocation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting equipment allocation decisions, operational constraints, or special resource requirements for this vessel call.

attributes.name: restow_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this container requires restowing or repositioning on the vessel to access underlying cargo or optimize stowage.

attributes.name: row_number
attributes.description: Transverse position identifier on the vessel indicating the row location for container stowage.

attributes.name: seal_number
