attributes.description: Reference to the vessel requiring towage assistance. Links to the vessel master data product for full vessel details.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Identification Number Scheme; SOLAS Chapter XI-1 Reg 3

attributes.name: vessel_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.vessel_master. Business justification: Towage planning and tug assignment calculations require vessel master data (LOA, beam, DWT, GRT) for bollard pull determination, tariff calculation, and P&I club verification. Removes denormalized ves

attributes.name: vessel_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.vessel_type. Business justification: Towage tariff calculation, tug count determination, and bollard pull requirements depend on vessel type classification (container, tanker, bulk carrier) for service specification and pricing. Vessel t

attributes.name: abort_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for aborting or cancelling the towage operation. Mandatory when service_outcome is 'aborted' or 'cancelled'. Used for root cause analysis and operational improvement.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter V; Port Incident Reporting Procedures

attributes.name: actual_commencement
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the towage operation commenced, defined as first tug line made fast to the vessel. Used for KPI measurement, billing, and SLA compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; Port Billing Tariff Schedule

attributes.name: actual_completion
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the towage operation was completed, defined as last tug line cast off from the vessel. Used for duration calculation, billing, and KPI reporting.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; Port Billing Tariff Schedule

attributes.name: billing_status
attributes.description: Current billing and invoicing status of the towage order. 'pending' = charge calculated but not yet invoiced; 'invoiced' = invoice raised; 'disputed' = charge under dispute; 'paid' = payment received; 'waived' = charge waived by port authority.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI Financial Accounting; Port Billing Procedures

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the towage order record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the towage charge amount (e.g., USD, EUR, SGD, AUD). Required for multi-currency port operations and financial reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI Financial Accounting

attributes.name: current_speed_knots
attributes.description: Recorded tidal current speed in knots at the berth or channel location at the time of towage. Critical environmental parameter influencing tug power requirements and safety assessment.
attributes.references: IHO Hydrographic Standards; PIANC Guidelines for Towage; SOLAS Chapter V

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the towage operation in minutes, calculated from actual_commencement to actual_completion. Used for billing, performance benchmarking, and port throughput analytics.
attributes.references: Port Billing Tariff Schedule; IAPH Port Performance Indicators

attributes.name: imdg_hazmat_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Hazardous Material Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the vessel is carrying International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) classified hazardous cargo at the time of towage. True = hazardous cargo on board. Influences tug safety protocols and emergency response readiness.
attributes.references: IMDG Code (IMO); SOLAS Chapter VII; MARPOL Annex III

tag_set.value: International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Hazardous Material Flag

attributes.name: min_bollard_pull_tonnes
attributes.description: Minimum total bollard pull force in metric tonnes required for the towage operation, calculated based on vessel DWT, environmental conditions, and port-specific towage assessment criteria.
attributes.references: PIANC Guidelines for Towage; IMO MSC Circular 1331; Bureau Veritas Tug Standards

attributes.name: order_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known human-readable reference number assigned to the towage order, used in communications with shipping agents, tug operators, and port authority. Format: TOW-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; Port Community System (PCS)

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the towage order. 'requested' = initial request received; 'confirmed' = tugs allocated and confirmed; 'in_progress' = towage operation underway; 'completed' = service successfully delivered; 'aborted' = commenced but terminated early; 'cancelled' = cancelled before commencement.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; IMO Resolution A.994(25)

attributes.name: port_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: United Nations Location Code (UN/LOCODE) Port Code
attributes.description: UN/LOCODE five-character port code identifying the port where the towage service is performed. Supports multi-port operations and regulatory reporting to IMO and national maritime authorities.
attributes.references: UN/LOCODE Standard (UNECE Recommendation 16); IMO FAL Convention

tag_set.value: United Nations Location Code (UN/LOCODE) Port Code

attributes.name: requested_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the towage service was formally requested by the shipping agent or vessel operator. Principal business event timestamp marking the start of the towage order lifecycle.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; IMO FAL Convention

attributes.name: safety_observation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a safety observation, near-miss, or safety concern was recorded during the towage operation. True = safety observation exists. Triggers mandatory safety review process per SOLAS and ISPS requirements.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter V; ISPS Code; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: safety_observation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text description of any safety observations, near-misses, or hazards identified during the towage operation. Populated when safety_observation_flag is True. Used for safety management system reporting.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter V; ISPS Code; ISO 45001; MARPOL Annex I

attributes.name: scheduled_commencement
attributes.description: Planned date and time for the towage operation to commence, aligned with the vessel's Estimated Time of Berthing (ETB) or Estimated Time of Departure (ETD) schedule.
attributes.references: VTMS Vessel Traffic Management System; IMO FAL Convention

attributes.name: service_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the towage service delivery. 'completed' = full service delivered successfully; 'aborted' = commenced but terminated before completion; 'cancelled' = cancelled before commencement; 'partial' = service partially delivered due to operational constraints.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; Port SLA Framework

attributes.name: shipping_line_code
attributes.description: Standard Carrier Alpha Code (SCAC) of the shipping line or vessel operator on whose behalf the towage is requested. Four-letter uppercase code per NMFTA standard.
attributes.references: NMFTA SCAC Code Standard; Port Community System (PCS)

attributes.name: special_instructions
attributes.description: Free-text field for any special operational instructions, constraints, or requirements for the towage operation, such as restricted manoeuvring areas, hazardous cargo considerations, or vessel-specific handling notes.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter V; IMDG Code; Port Operations Manual

attributes.name: tariff_code
attributes.description: Port tariff code applied to calculate the towage service charge. References the applicable tariff schedule item for the towage type, vessel class, and service conditions.
attributes.references: Port Tariff Schedule; SAP S/4HANA CO Controlling; IAPH Port Tariff Guidelines

attributes.name: towage_charge_amount
attributes.description: Gross towage service charge amount in the port's base currency, calculated per the applicable port tariff schedule based on vessel GRT, towage type, duration, and number of tugs. Used for billing and revenue reporting.
attributes.references: Port Tariff Schedule; SAP S/4HANA FI Billing; IAPH Port Tariff Guidelines

attributes.name: towage_type
attributes.description: Classification of the towage operation by purpose. 'arrival' = vessel inbound to berth; 'departure' = vessel outbound from berth; 'shifting' = vessel moving between berths within port; 'emergency' = unplanned emergency towage; 'dry_dock' = towage to/from dry dock facility.
attributes.references: PIANC Guidelines for Towage; IMO Resolution A.994(25)

attributes.name: tug_attachment_bow
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tug is required to be attached at the bow (forward) of the vessel as part of the towage configuration. True = bow tug required.
attributes.references: PIANC Guidelines for Towage; Port Towage Procedures Manual

attributes.name: tug_attachment_breast
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tug is required to be attached breast (alongside) the vessel as part of the towage configuration. True = breast tug required.
attributes.references: PIANC Guidelines for Towage; Port Towage Procedures Manual

attributes.name: tug_attachment_stern
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tug is required to be attached at the stern (aft) of the vessel as part of the towage configuration. True = stern tug required.
attributes.references: PIANC Guidelines for Towage; Port Towage Procedures Manual

attributes.name: tugs_assigned
attributes.description: Actual number of tug vessels assigned and dispatched for the towage operation. May differ from tugs_required if operational adjustments are made.
attributes.references: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; PIANC Guidelines for Towage

attributes.name: tugs_required
attributes.description: Total number of tug vessels required to safely execute the towage operation as determined by the port's towage assessment based on vessel LOA, DWT, wind, and current conditions.
attributes.references: PIANC Guidelines for Towage; Port Towage Regulations

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the towage order record was last modified. Used for change tracking, incremental data loads, and audit compliance.

attributes.name: visibility_category
attributes.description: Meteorological visibility category at the time of towage commencement. 'good' = >5nm; 'moderate' = 2-5nm; 'poor' = 0.5-2nm; 'very_poor' = <0.5nm. Used for safety risk assessment and incident reporting.
attributes.references: WMO Visibility Classification; SOLAS Chapter V; COLREGS Rule 19

attributes.name: wind_direction
attributes.description: Recorded wind direction using 16-point compass bearing at the time of towage commencement. Used in conjunction with wind speed for environmental condition assessment and safety reporting.
attributes.references: WMO Meteorological Standards; SOLAS Chapter V; Environmental Monitoring System (EMS)

attributes.name: wind_speed_knots
attributes.description: Recorded wind speed in knots at the time of towage commencement. Environmental condition captured for safety assessment, incident investigation, and towage risk analysis.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter V; IMO MSC Circular 1331; Environmental Monitoring System (EMS)

products.name: tug
products.description: Master record for each tug vessel operated or contracted at the port, including tug name, IMO number, flag state, bollard pull rating (tonnes), engine power (kW), tug type (ASD, conventional, voith), LOA, beam, draught, fire-fighting class (FiFi), escort tug certification, current operational status, and owning/operating company. SSOT for tug asset identity.
products.reference: IMO Ship Identification / Port Tug Registry

attributes.name: tug_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each tug vessel record in the port's marine services master data. Primary key for the tug asset identity table. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Identification Number Scheme; ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.agreement. Business justification: Tugs operated under concession/lease agreements with port authority or third-party operators. Required for concession tracking, performance bond management, revenue share calculation, and contract com

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Tugs are capital assets requiring depreciation, maintenance capex tracking, insurance valuation, and asset register compliance. Core fixed asset management requirement for maritime fleet financial rep

attributes.name: flag_state_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.flag_state. Business justification: Tug regulatory compliance, PSC inspection targeting, and flag state survey requirements depend on flag state master data (PSC targeting factor, flag state authority, MOU membership) for operational co

attributes.name: port_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.port_asset. Business justification: Tugs are both operational vessels (marine domain) and depreciable capital assets (asset domain). Asset register tracks acquisition cost, depreciation, book value, disposal planning, and insurance valu

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Tugs with ownership_type = 'contracted' or 'leased' are provided by external vendors. This FK enables linking contracted tug assets to vendor records for contract management, invoicing, and performanc

attributes.name: vessel_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.vessel_master. Business justification: Tugs are vessels requiring vessel master data (classification society, P&I club, flag state authority, PSC inspection history) for regulatory compliance, insurance verification, and operational status

attributes.name: vessel_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.vessel_type. Business justification: Tug classification (harbor tug, ocean-going tug, AHTS, escort tug) requires vessel type master data for capability categorization, tariff classification, and service assignment matching. Tug_type fiel

attributes.name: ahts_capable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Anchor Handling and Towing Supply (AHTS) Capable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the tug vessel is equipped and certified for anchor handling and towing supply (AHTS) operations, including offshore anchor deployment and retrieval. True = AHTS capable; False = harbour towage only. Relevant for ports serving offshore oil and gas support operations.
attributes.references: Classification Society AHTS Notation Rules; IMO Guidelines for Offshore Supply Vessels

tag_set.value: Anchor Handling and Towing Supply (AHTS) Capable Flag

attributes.name: ais_transponder_class
attributes.description: Class of the Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponder fitted on the tug vessel. Class A transponders are mandatory for SOLAS vessels and provide full dynamic data; Class B transponders are used on smaller non-SOLAS vessels with reduced transmission frequency. Determines the vessel's real-time tracking capability within the port's VTS system.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19; ITU-R M.1371; IMO Resolution MSC.74(69); VTS Operational Procedures

attributes.name: beam_m
attributes.description: Maximum breadth (beam) of the tug vessel in metres measured at the widest point of the hull. Used in navigation clearance calculations, dry dock planning, and assessing compatibility with port infrastructure such as lock chambers and fendering systems.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Measurement Convention; PIANC Harbour Design Standards

attributes.name: bollard_pull_tonnes
attributes.description: Certified static bollard pull force of the tug in metric tonnes, as measured and certified under controlled test conditions. The principal performance metric used to match tug capability to vessel assistance requirements based on the assisted vessel's DWT, LOA, and environmental conditions. Critical for berth allocation planning and safe towage operations.
attributes.references: IMO MSC/Circ.884 Tug Bollard Pull Certification; PIANC Working Group Reports; ISO 3828 Bollard Pull Test

attributes.name: build_shipyard
attributes.description: Name of the shipyard where the tug vessel was constructed. Retained for asset provenance records, warranty claims, technical documentation retrieval, and historical maintenance reference in Maximo Asset Management.
attributes.references: Maximo Asset Management Asset Record; IMO Ship Construction Certificate

attributes.name: call_sign
attributes.description: International radio call sign assigned to the tug vessel by the flag state telecommunications authority. Used for VHF radio communications with Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) and port control during towage and escort operations.
attributes.references: ITU Radio Regulations; IMO SOLAS Chapter IV; VTS Operational Procedures

attributes.name: class_notation
attributes.description: Full classification notation string assigned by the classification society, describing the vessel's structural class, machinery class, and any additional notations (e.g., fire-fighting, escort, ice class). Provides a concise technical summary of the vessel's certified capabilities and construction standards.
attributes.references: IACS Unified Requirements; Classification Society Rules for Tugs and Workboats

attributes.name: class_survey_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the next mandatory classification society survey (annual, intermediate, or special/renewal) must be completed to maintain the vessel's class certificate in good standing. Used in maintenance planning and operational availability forecasting in Maximo Asset Management.
attributes.references: IACS Survey Requirements; Classification Society Survey Schedules; IMO SOLAS Chapter I

attributes.name: classification_society
attributes.description: Name of the international classification society (e.g., Lloyd's Register, DNV, Bureau Veritas, ABS, ClassNK) that has classed the tug vessel and issues its class certificates. Determines the survey regime, structural standards, and equipment certification applicable to the vessel.
attributes.references: IACS (International Association of Classification Societies) Member Rules; IMO SOLAS Chapter II

attributes.name: commissioned_date
attributes.description: Date on which the tug vessel was formally commissioned into service at the port, either as a new build delivery or upon commencement of a charter/contract arrangement. Marks the start of the vessel's operational lifecycle record in Maximo Asset Management and the port's marine services SSOT.
attributes.references: Maximo Asset Management Asset Commissioning; IMO Ship Delivery Certificate; SAP S/4HANA PM Asset Master

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current charter or service contract for the tug vessel is scheduled to expire. Nullable for open-ended arrangements. Used to trigger contract renewal workflows and ensure continuity of towage service capacity planning.
attributes.references: BIMCO Charter Party Terms; SAP S/4HANA FI Contract Management

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current charter or service contract for the tug vessel became effective. Applicable for chartered or contracted tugs. Used in commercial management, billing cycle determination, and contract renewal planning in the source system
attributes.references: BIMCO Charter Party Terms; SAP S/4HANA FI Contract Management

attributes.name: crew_complement
attributes.description: Minimum number of crew members required to safely operate the tug vessel as specified in the vessel's Safe Manning Certificate issued by the flag state. Used in workforce planning, shift rostering, and compliance with ILO Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006) crewing requirements.
attributes.references: IMO Safe Manning Certificate (SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 14); ILO Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006); National Maritime Safety Authority

attributes.name: decommissioned_date
attributes.description: Date on which the tug vessel was formally withdrawn from service at the port, either permanently or for an extended lay-up period. Nullable for vessels currently in service. Used to close the asset lifecycle record and trigger final compliance and financial close-out processes.
attributes.references: Maximo Asset Management Asset Retirement; SAP S/4HANA PM Asset Lifecycle; IMO Ship Recycling Convention

attributes.name: draught_m
attributes.description: Maximum operational draught of the tug vessel in metres. Used to assess navigability in shallow harbour areas, tidal windows for operations, and compliance with port water depth restrictions. Critical for safe operations in ports with tidal or dredging constraints.
attributes.references: IMO Load Line Convention; IHO Hydrographic Survey Standards; PIANC Dredging Guidelines

attributes.name: engine_power_kw
attributes.description: Total installed main engine power output of the tug vessel measured in kilowatts (kW). Used alongside bollard pull rating to assess tug capability, fuel consumption planning, and compliance with port emission standards. Sourced from the vessel's engine certificate and classification society records.
attributes.references: IMO MARPOL Annex VI NOx Technical Code; Classification Society Engine Certification; ISO 3046 Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines

attributes.name: escort_bollard_pull_tonnes
attributes.description: Certified escort bollard pull force in metric tonnes, measured under dynamic escort conditions as distinct from static bollard pull. Applicable only to escort-certified tugs. Used to determine the maximum DWT of tankers and gas carriers the tug can safely escort through the port approach channel.
attributes.references: IACS Unified Requirement W31; IMO MSC Guidelines on Escort Tug Operations

attributes.name: escort_certified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the tug vessel holds a valid escort tug certification from its classification society, confirming it meets the structural, stability, and equipment standards required for escort towage of large tankers and gas carriers in restricted waterways. True = certified for escort operations; False = not certified.
attributes.references: IACS Unified Requirement W31 Escort Tug; IMO MSC Guidelines on Escort Tug Operations; PIANC Escort Tug Standards

attributes.name: fifi_class
attributes.description: IMO/classification society fire-fighting system class notation of the tug vessel. FiFi1 denotes basic fire-fighting capability; FiFi1+WS includes water spray; FiFi2 and FiFi3 denote progressively higher capacity systems. 'none' indicates no certified fire-fighting equipment. Determines eligibility for fire-fighting standby duties and emergency response assignments in the port.
attributes.references: IMO MSC/Circ.1239 Fire-Fighting Systems; SOLAS Chapter II-2; Classification Society FiFi Notation Rules

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Primary fuel type used by the tug vessel's main engines. HFO = Heavy Fuel Oil; MGO = Marine Gas Oil; MDO = Marine Diesel Oil; LNG = Liquefied Natural Gas; methanol = methanol fuel; hybrid = dual-fuel or battery-hybrid arrangement. Used in emissions reporting under MARPOL Annex VI, GHG tracking, and port environmental management.
attributes.references: MARPOL Annex VI; IMO MEPC GHG Strategy; Environmental Monitoring System (EMS); ISO 14001

attributes.name: gross_tonnage
attributes.description: Gross Registered Tonnage (GRT) of the tug vessel as certified under the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships. Used for port dues calculation, PSC inspection scheduling, and regulatory reporting to maritime authorities.
attributes.references: IMO Tonnage Convention 1969; IAPH Port Dues Tariff Framework

attributes.name: home_port
attributes.description: Name of the port or terminal at which the tug vessel is normally based and from which it is dispatched for towage and marine service operations. Used in operational planning, crew logistics, and maintenance scheduling within the port's marine services management system.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Operations Guidelines; VTMS Vessel Registry

attributes.name: ice_class
attributes.description: Ice class notation assigned by the classification society indicating the tug vessel's structural capability to operate in ice-covered waters. Ranges from 'IA Super' (highest) to 'ID' (lowest ice class) or 'none' for no ice capability. Relevant for ports in seasonal ice regions and for compliance with IACS Polar Class requirements.
attributes.references: IACS Unified Requirements for Polar Class Ships; Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules; IMO Polar Code

attributes.name: isps_cert_expiry
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Certificate Expiry Date
attributes.description: Expiry date of the International Ship Security Certificate (ISSC) issued under the ISPS Code. Confirms the vessel has an approved Ship Security Plan and complies with SOLAS Chapter XI-2 security requirements. Required for port access and monitored by port facility security officers.
attributes.references: ISPS Code (SOLAS Chapter XI-2); IMO MSC/Circ.1192; National Maritime Security Authority

tag_set.value: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Certificate Expiry Date

attributes.name: last_dry_dock_date
attributes.description: Date on which the tug vessel most recently completed a dry docking for hull inspection, underwater maintenance, and classification society survey. Used in maintenance planning to calculate the next scheduled dry dock and assess hull condition for operational readiness.
attributes.references: Classification Society Dry Dock Survey Requirements; Maximo Asset Management Preventive Maintenance; IACS Survey Guidelines

attributes.name: loa_m
attributes.description: Length Overall (LOA) of the tug vessel in metres, measured from the foremost point to the aftermost point of the hull. Used in berth planning, harbour navigation clearance assessments, and determining operational constraints within the port basin.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Measurement Convention; PIANC Harbour Design Standards; IHO Hydrographic Survey Standards

attributes.name: marpol_cert_expiry
attributes.description: Expiry date of the vessel's MARPOL compliance certificate (International Oil Pollution Prevention Certificate or equivalent), confirming the tug meets IMO Marine Pollution Convention requirements for prevention of pollution from ships. Monitored for environmental compliance and PSC inspection readiness.
attributes.references: MARPOL 73/78 Annex I; IMO MEPC Resolutions; Environmental Monitoring System (EMS)

attributes.name: max_speed_knots
attributes.description: Maximum service speed of the tug vessel in knots under normal operating conditions. Used in marine service scheduling to calculate transit times to vessel rendezvous positions, optimise tug dispatch timing, and assess response capability for emergency towage.
attributes.references: Classification Society Sea Trial Records; IAPH Tug Performance Standards

attributes.name: mmsi_number
attributes.description: Nine-digit Maritime Mobile Service Identity number used for Automatic Identification System (AIS) transmissions and Digital Selective Calling (DSC) communications. Enables real-time vessel tracking via VTS and port monitoring systems.
attributes.references: ITU-R M.585; IMO Resolution MSC.74(69) Annex 3; SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19

attributes.name: tug_name
attributes.description: Official registered name of the tug vessel as recorded on the vessel's certificate of registry. Used as the primary human-readable identity label in port operations, VTS communications, and marine service scheduling.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Registration Standards; IAPH Port Operations Guidelines

attributes.name: net_tonnage
attributes.description: Net Registered Tonnage (NRT) of the tug vessel as certified under the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships. Represents the vessel's earning capacity and is used in certain port tariff calculations and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: IMO Tonnage Convention 1969; IAPH Port Dues Tariff Framework

attributes.name: next_dry_dock_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the tug vessel's next dry docking. Used in long-term maintenance scheduling, operational availability planning, and budget forecasting for CAPEX dry dock expenditure in the source system
attributes.references: Classification Society Survey Schedules; Maximo Asset Management Preventive Maintenance Planning; SAP S/4HANA PM

attributes.name: official_number
attributes.description: National official registration number assigned by the flag state maritime authority at the port of registry. Complements the IMO number as a domestic regulatory identifier used in national maritime administration and port authority records.
attributes.references: National Maritime Safety Authority Registration Regulations; Flag State Ship Registration Act

attributes.name: operating_company
attributes.description: Legal name of the company responsible for the day-to-day commercial and technical management and operation of the tug vessel. May be the same as the owning company or a contracted towage operator. Used in service agreements, billing, and ISM Code compliance documentation.
attributes.references: IMO ISM Code (International Safety Management); SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master; IAPH Towage Service Agreements

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle and availability status of the tug vessel within port marine services operations. 'available' indicates ready for dispatch; 'assigned' indicates currently engaged on a towage or escort job; 'maintenance' indicates undergoing scheduled or unscheduled maintenance; 'out_of_service' indicates temporarily non-operational; 'laid_up' indicates long-term decommissioning or storage.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Operations Guidelines; Maximo Asset Management Lifecycle States; IMO ISM Code

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Classification of the commercial arrangement under which the port or towage operator controls the tug vessel. 'owned' = port authority or operator owns the vessel outright; 'bareboat_charter' = vessel chartered without crew; 'time_charter' = vessel chartered with crew for a fixed period; 'contracted' = third-party towage company provides the vessel under a service contract.
attributes.references: BIMCO Standard Charter Party Forms; SAP S/4HANA FI Contract Management; IAPH Commercial Guidelines

attributes.name: owning_company
attributes.description: Legal name of the company that holds registered ownership of the tug vessel. May differ from the operating company in cases of bareboat charter or leasing arrangements. Used in commercial contracts, insurance documentation, P&I Club notifications, and port authority vessel registration records.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Registration; P&I Club Membership Rules; SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master

attributes.name: pi_club
attributes.description: Name of the Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club providing third-party liability insurance coverage for the tug vessel. P&I insurance covers liabilities arising from towage operations including collision, pollution, and crew injury. Required for port entry and towage service authorisation under ISPS and port authority regulations.
attributes.references: International Group of P&I Clubs Rules; IMO SOLAS; IAPH Port Entry Requirements

attributes.name: pi_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current P&I Club insurance certificate expires. Used to trigger renewal alerts and ensure continuous insurance coverage. Tugs with expired P&I cover must not be dispatched for towage operations under port authority rules.
attributes.references: International Group of P&I Clubs Rules; IAPH Port Entry Requirements; IMO ISM Code

attributes.name: pi_policy_number
attributes.description: Policy or certificate number of the current P&I Club insurance cover for the tug vessel. Used in incident reporting, claims management, and port authority compliance verification. Required to be presented during PSC inspections and port entry clearance.
attributes.references: International Group of P&I Clubs Certificate of Entry; IMO ISM Code; ISPS Code

attributes.name: port_of_registry
attributes.description: Name of the port where the tug vessel is officially registered as recorded on the vessel's certificate of registry. Displayed on the vessel's stern and used in official maritime documentation and PSC inspections.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Registration Standards; UNCLOS Article 91

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for recording operational notes, special conditions, known limitations, or temporary restrictions applicable to the tug vessel that are not captured in structured fields. Examples include temporary equipment deficiencies, operational restrictions imposed by the classification society, or special port authority conditions.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Operations Guidelines; IMO ISM Code Deficiency Reporting

attributes.name: safety_management_cert_expiry
attributes.description: Expiry date of the Safety Management Certificate (SMC) issued under the ISM Code, confirming the vessel's safety management system complies with IMO requirements. Tugs operating under the ISM Code must maintain a valid SMC. Used in compliance monitoring and PSC inspection preparation.
attributes.references: IMO ISM Code (Resolution A.741(18)); SOLAS Chapter IX; PSC Inspection Procedures

attributes.name: tug_type
attributes.description: Classification of the tug vessel by propulsion and manoeuvring system design. ASD (Azimuth Stern Drive) tugs offer 360-degree thrust; conventional tugs use fixed propellers; voith tugs use Voith-Schneider cycloidal propellers; tractor tugs use forward-mounted azimuth drives; rotor tugs use a hybrid arrangement. Determines operational capability and assignment suitability for specific towage tasks.
attributes.references: IAPH Tug Classification Standards; IMO MSC Circular on Tug Operations

attributes.name: year_built
attributes.description: Calendar year in which the tug vessel was constructed and delivered from the shipyard. Used in asset lifecycle management, maintenance planning, insurance valuation, and assessing compliance with age-related regulatory requirements under PSC and flag state rules.
attributes.references: IMO Ship Construction Standards; Maximo Asset Management Lifecycle; Classification Society Rules

products.name: mooring_operation
products.description: Transactional record for each mooring and unmooring service performed at a berth, buoy, or dolphin within port waters. Captures mooring gang assigned, number and configuration of lines deployed (head, breast, spring, stern), mooring equipment used (capstans, bollards, quick-release hooks), SWL compliance verification, commencement and completion timestamps, tide height and weather conditions, vessel movement type (arrival, departure, shift), and any mooring irregularities or safety observations. SSOT for all mooring service delivery events.

attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each mooring or unmooring service event recorded in the port. Primary key for the mooring_operation data product.
attributes.references: IMO Resolution A.1045(27) — Pilotage and Mooring Services

attributes.name: billable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this mooring operation is subject to a tariff charge to the vessel operator or shipping agent. Non-billable operations may include emergency services or internal port movements.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Tariff Standards; NAVIS N4 Billing Module; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: bollards_used_count
attributes.description: Number of shore-side bollards engaged during the mooring operation. Used for infrastructure utilisation tracking, SWL compliance, and berth equipment maintenance scheduling in Maximo.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); Maximo Asset Management — Berth Equipment

attributes.name: breast_lines_count
attributes.description: Number of breast lines (mooring lines running perpendicular to the vessel's centreline) deployed during the mooring operation. Critical for lateral restraint and SWL compliance verification.

attributes.name: capstans_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether shore-side capstans (powered mooring winches) were utilised during this mooring operation to assist in line tensioning and vessel positioning.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); Port Equipment Maintenance Standards

attributes.name: charge_amount
attributes.description: Gross charge amount levied for this mooring operation in the port's operating currency, as calculated from the applicable tariff code and gang size/duration. Used for revenue recognition and billing reconciliation.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Tariff Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI Revenue Accounting; Port Tariff Schedule

attributes.name: commencement_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the mooring operation physically commenced, i.e., when the first line was passed or the unmooring sequence began. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Convention; IAPH Port Operations Standards; NAVIS N4 Billing Module

attributes.name: completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the mooring operation was fully completed, i.e., all lines secured and vessel confirmed fast, or all lines cast off and vessel clear. Used for duration calculation and billing.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Convention; IAPH Port Operations Standards; NAVIS N4 Billing Module

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this mooring operation record was first created in the system, representing the audit trail creation point. Used for data lineage and compliance auditing.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Date and Time Standards; ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the charge amount (e.g., USD, AUD, SGD). Supports multi-currency port operations and financial reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: current_speed_knots
attributes.description: Recorded water current speed in knots at the berth location during the mooring operation. Relevant for mooring load assessment and safety compliance.
attributes.references: IHO Hydrographic Standards; PIANC MarCom Report 121

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in minutes from commencement to completion of the mooring operation. Captured as a business field from the operational system for KPI reporting and SLA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Performance Indicators; PMIS KPI Framework

attributes.name: gang_size
attributes.description: Number of mooring personnel deployed for this operation. Used for resource planning, billing calculation, and compliance with minimum manning requirements.
attributes.references: ILO Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006); Port Labour Standards

attributes.name: gang_supervisor
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the supervisor leading the mooring gang for this operation. Used for accountability, incident investigation, and performance management.
attributes.references: ILO Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006); ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: head_lines_count
attributes.description: Number of head lines (forward mooring lines running ahead of the vessel) deployed during the mooring operation. Part of the line configuration record for SWL compliance and operational audit.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); SOLAS Chapter II-1

attributes.name: incident_ref
attributes.description: Reference number of the formal marine incident report raised in connection with this mooring operation. Populated when incident_reported is true. Links to the marine incident management record.
attributes.references: IMO Casualty Investigation Code (MSC.255(84)); SOLAS Chapter XI-1

attributes.name: incident_reported
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal marine incident report was raised as a result of this mooring operation. When true, the incident is tracked in the marine incident management system aligned with SOLAS and MARPOL requirements.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter XI-1 Reg 6; MARPOL; IMO Casualty Investigation Code (Res. MSC.255(84))

attributes.name: irregularity_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of any mooring irregularity, safety observation, equipment deficiency, or non-conformance observed during the operation. Populated when irregularity_observed is true. Used for incident investigation and safety reporting.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter II-1; ISO 45001; MARPOL Annex I; ISPS Code

attributes.name: irregularity_observed
attributes.description: Indicates whether any mooring irregularity, safety observation, or non-conformance was recorded during this operation. When true, details are captured in the irregularity_description field.
attributes.references: SOLAS Chapter II-1; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; ISPS Code

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this mooring operation record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Date and Time Standards; ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security

attributes.name: line_material_type
attributes.description: Material composition of the mooring lines used in this operation. Relevant for SWL compliance verification and equipment condition assessment. HMPE = High Modulus Polyethylene (e.g., Dyneema).
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); ISO 1140 Fibre Ropes

attributes.name: mooring_location_type
attributes.description: Classification of the physical mooring location type where the vessel is secured: conventional berth alongside a quay, single-point or multi-buoy mooring, dolphin structure, jetty, or open quay face.
attributes.references: PIANC MarCom Report 121; Port Infrastructure Classification Standards

attributes.name: operation_ref
attributes.description: Externally-known business reference number assigned to this mooring or unmooring service event, used in billing, port management information system (PMIS) records, and inter-agency communications.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Operations Standards; PMIS Reference Numbering Convention

attributes.name: operation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the mooring operation, tracking progression from planning through execution to completion or cancellation.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Operations Standards; SOLAS Chapter V — Safety of Navigation

attributes.name: operation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the mooring service performed: mooring (securing vessel on arrival), unmooring (releasing vessel on departure), shifting (moving vessel between berths), or re-mooring (re-securing after adjustment).
attributes.references: IMO Resolution A.1045(27); PIANC Working Group Reports

attributes.name: pi_club_notified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club Notified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the vessel's Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club insurer was notified of an incident or irregularity arising from this mooring operation. Relevant for liability and insurance claim management.
attributes.references: International Group of P&I Clubs Rules; IMO Casualty Investigation Code

tag_set.value: Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club Notified Flag

attributes.name: pilot_on_board
attributes.description: Indicates whether a marine pilot was on board the vessel during this mooring operation. Relevant for coordination between pilotage and mooring services and for incident liability determination.
attributes.references: IMO Resolution A.960(23) — Recommendations on Training and Certification of Maritime Pilots; SOLAS Chapter V Reg 23

attributes.name: quick_release_hooks_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether quick-release mooring hooks were deployed during this operation. Quick-release hooks are critical safety equipment for emergency vessel release and are tracked for compliance and maintenance purposes.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); PIANC MarCom Report 121

attributes.name: spring_lines_count
attributes.description: Number of spring lines (mooring lines running at an angle fore and aft to prevent surging) deployed during the mooring operation. Part of the full line configuration record.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); SOLAS Chapter II-1

attributes.name: stern_lines_count
attributes.description: Number of stern lines (aft mooring lines running astern of the vessel) deployed during the mooring operation. Part of the line configuration record for SWL compliance and operational audit.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); SOLAS Chapter II-1

attributes.name: swl_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether all mooring lines and equipment used in this operation were verified to be within their Safe Working Load (SWL) limits at the time of the operation. Mandatory compliance check per OCIMF and port safety regulations.
attributes.references: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4); ISO 45001; SOLAS Chapter II-1

attributes.name: tariff_code
attributes.description: Port tariff code applied to this mooring operation for billing purposes, referencing the applicable rate schedule in the port's tariff book. Used in the source system integration.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Tariff Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI Billing; Port Tariff Schedule

attributes.name: tide_height_m
attributes.description: Recorded tide height in metres above chart datum at the time of the mooring operation commencement. Critical for under-keel clearance assessment and mooring line angle calculations.
attributes.references: IHO S-44 Standards for Hydrographic Surveys; National Maritime Safety Authority Tidal Data

attributes.name: total_lines_count
attributes.description: Total number of mooring lines deployed across all configurations (head, stern, breast, spring) for this operation. Used for equipment inventory reconciliation and billing.

attributes.name: towage_assist_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether tug assistance was used in conjunction with this mooring operation to manoeuvre the vessel to or from the berth. Used for service coordination and billing linkage to towage operations.
attributes.references: IAPH Port Operations Standards; IMO Resolution A.1045(27)

attributes.name: vessel_movement_type
attributes.description: Indicates the vessel movement context for which the mooring service is being performed: arrival at berth, departure from berth, or an intra-port shift between berths or positions.
attributes.references: VTMS Vessel Movement Classification; IMO FAL Convention

attributes.name: visibility_category
attributes.description: Categorical assessment of meteorological visibility conditions at the time of the mooring operation: good (>5nm), moderate (2-5nm), poor (0.5-2nm), very poor (<0.5nm). Used for safety risk assessment.
attributes.references: IMO Resolution A.893(21) — Guidelines for Voyage Planning; SOLAS Chapter V

attributes.name: wind_direction
attributes.description: Compass direction from which the wind was blowing at the berth location during the mooring operation, expressed as a 16-point compass bearing. Used for safety assessment and incident investigation.
attributes.references: WMO Meteorological Standards; SOLAS Chapter V — Meteorological Services

attributes.name: wind_speed_knots
attributes.description: Recorded wind speed in knots at the berth location at the time of the mooring operation. Used for safety assessment, incident investigation, and environmental condition logging.
attributes.references: WMO Beaufort Wind Scale; SOLAS Chapter V — Meteorological Services; EMS Environmental Monitoring

products.name: launch_dispatch
products.description: SSOT for the complete launch boat service including fleet asset management and operational dispatch. Captures launch boat master data (vessel name, registration, hull type, engine configuration, passenger capacity, SWL for cargo, certification status, survey dates, assigned berth/jetty, operational availability) and each dispatch event (purpose — pilot transfer, crew change, chandler delivery, inspection, surveyor boarding — vessel served, departure/return times, sea state, passengers carried, coxswain identity, safety observations). Supports 24/7 pilot transfer operations and anchorage service delivery.
products.reference: SOLAS Chapter III — Life-Saving Appliances / Port Launch Operations

products.name: marpol_operation
products.description: SSOT for all MARPOL-regulated compliance activities within port waters, consolidating operational records, waste reception transactions, and port reception facility master data. Captures vessel, activity type, waste category, quantity, disposal method, receiving facility details (type, capacity, licensed contractor, inspection status), waste manifest references, collection timestamps, and port authority sign-off. products.name: pilot_channel_authorisation
products.description: This association product represents the formal authorisation granted to a licensed marine pilot to conduct pilotage operations within a specific navigable channel or fairway. It captures the regulatory approval process, vessel size limits specific to the pilot-channel combination, examination results, passage experience, and authorisation validity periods. Each record links one pilot to one channel with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific authorisation relationship.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, pilots must obtain specific authorisation for each channel or fairway they are qualified to navigate, based on channel-specific examinations, passage experience, and vessel size limits. A single pilot holds authorisations for multiple channels (enabling operational flexibility), and each channel requires multiple authorised pilots to ensure 24/7 coverage and operational continuity. The authorisation itself is a regulated business entity with its own lifecycle (grant date, expiry, status, examination records, passage counts) that is actively managed by port authorities.

products.name: pilot_vessel_type_endorsement
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory endorsement relationship between a licensed marine pilot and a specific vessel type classification. It captures the pilot's authorization, training, and operational limits for conducting pilotage operations on vessels of a specific type. Each record links one pilot to one vessel type with endorsement-specific attributes including dates, limits, training status, and regulatory compliance data that exist only in the context of this specific endorsement.. Existence Justification: In maritime pilotage operations, pilots hold multiple vessel type endorsements (container ships, tankers, LNG carriers, bulk carriers, etc.), and each vessel type can be piloted by multiple qualified pilots. Licensing authorities track endorsement-specific training, operational limits (LOA, DWT), simulator training completion, expiry dates, and restrictions for each pilot-vessel type combination. This is an actively managed regulatory compliance relationship where endorsements are issued, renewed, suspended, and tracked independently.

products.name: surveyor_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the contractual authorization between a marine surveyor and a commercial agreement. It captures the specific scope, rates, and terms under which a surveyor is authorized to perform survey services under a given agreement. Each record links one surveyor to one agreement with attributes that exist only in the context of this authorization relationship, including authorized survey types, rate overrides, validity periods, exclusivity arrangements, and performance tracking.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, commercial agreements (with shipping lines, stevedoring companies, marine service providers) frequently establish surveyor panels authorizing multiple surveyors to perform various survey types under agreement-specific terms. A single surveyor operates under multiple agreements with different clients, and each agreement authorizes multiple surveyors to ensure coverage, specialization, and redundancy. The authorization relationship itself carries business-critical data including authorized survey types, negotiated rates, validity periods, exclusivity arrangements, and performance tracking that belongs neither to the surveyor master record nor the agreement master record.

attributes.description: Indicates whether this route has tidal restrictions that affect vessel transit windows. True if route requires specific tidal conditions, false otherwise.

attributes.description: Indicates whether this route has weather-related operational restrictions. True if route is subject to closure or restrictions during adverse weather conditions.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: The geographic latitude coordinate of the berth center point in decimal degrees. Used for vessel navigation, VTS (Vessel Traffic Service) integration, and GIS-based port layout planning in AVEVA Marine Engineering.

attributes.name: length_m
attributes.description: The total usable length of the berth measured in meters along the quay wall. This is the maximum continuous length available for vessel mooring and determines the LOA (Length Overall) capacity.

attributes.name: loa_capacity_m
attributes.description: The maximum Length Overall (LOA) of a vessel that can be safely accommodated at this berth, measured in meters. This is a critical constraint for vessel planning and berth allocation in NAVIS N4 and TOPS Expert TOS.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: The geographic longitude coordinate of the berth center point in decimal degrees. Used for vessel navigation, VTS (Vessel Traffic Service) integration, and GIS-based port layout planning in AVEVA Marine Engineering.

attributes.name: max_draft_m
attributes.description: The maximum vessel draft (depth of the vessel below the waterline) that can be safely accommodated at this berth, measured in meters. This is constrained by the water depth alongside the berth and channel depth.

attributes.name: max_dwt_tonnes
attributes.description: The maximum Deadweight Tonnage (DWT) of a vessel that can be accommodated at this berth, measured in metric tonnes. DWT represents the total weight a vessel can safely carry including cargo, fuel, crew, and provisions.

attributes.name: mooring_fitting_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of mooring fitting types installed at this berth beyond bollards, such as hooks, rings, cleats, or quick-release hooks. Different vessel types and mooring configurations require different fitting types.

attributes.name: berth_name
attributes.description: The common name or designation of the berth, often referencing location or purpose (e.g., Container Terminal North Berth 1, Bulk Cargo Berth A).

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next planned preventive maintenance activity for this berth. Preventive maintenance includes fender replacement, bollard inspection, quay wall repairs, and equipment servicing. Sourced from Maximo Asset Management maintenance plans.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the berth. Operational berths are available for vessel scheduling, under_maintenance berths are temporarily unavailable, out_of_service berths are closed for extended periods, planned berths are under construction, and decommissioned berths are permanently retired.

attributes.name: rail_connection_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth has direct rail connection for intermodal cargo transfer. Rail connectivity is critical for inland container depots (ICD) and bulk cargo operations.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this berth record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this berth record was last modified. Updated whenever any attribute value changes. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit purposes.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, operational constraints, or historical information about this berth that do not fit into structured fields. Used by port operations and planning teams.

attributes.name: shore_crane_count
attributes.description: The number of shore-based cranes (STS - Ship-to-Shore cranes, QC - Quay Cranes, or MHC - Mobile Harbour Cranes) assigned to or available at this berth for cargo handling operations. Critical for container terminal berths and determines throughput capacity.

attributes.name: shore_power_available_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether shore power (cold ironing) is available at this berth. Shore power allows vessels to shut down auxiliary engines while berthed, reducing emissions and noise. Increasingly required for environmental compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 14001 Environmental Management, IMO MARPOL Annex VI

attributes.name: shore_power_capacity_kw
attributes.description: The total electrical power capacity available for shore power connection at this berth, measured in kilowatts (kW). Null if shore power is not available. Typical container vessel shore power requirements range from 1,000 to 10,000 kW.

attributes.name: tidal_constraint_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth has operational constraints due to tidal conditions. True indicates that vessel movements (arrival, departure, or cargo operations) are restricted to specific tidal windows.

attributes.name: tidal_range_m
attributes.description: The average tidal range (difference between high tide and low tide) at this berth location, measured in meters. Tidal constraints impact vessel scheduling, particularly for vessels with drafts close to the maximum depth.

attributes.name: warehouse_proximity_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this berth has direct or immediate proximity to covered warehouse facilities. Important for general cargo and break-bulk operations requiring weather-protected storage.

attributes.name: water_depth_alongside_m
attributes.description: The measured water depth alongside the berth at chart datum, measured in meters. This depth is maintained through regular dredging operations and determines the maximum draft capacity. Sourced from channel depth surveys and dredging records.

products.name: quay_wall

Captures wall type (gravity, sheet pile, caisson, piled), construction material, year built, total length, design load capacity (kN/m²), current structural condition rating, last structural inspection date, design standard, tidal range exposure, and associated berth references. Supports AVEVA Marine Engineering integration and CAPEX infrastructure project planning.

attributes.name: design_depth_m

SSOT for port layout, zone capacity planning, and terminal configuration management.

attributes.name: zone_manager_employee_id

attributes.name: access_control_system
attributes.description: Technology used to control personnel and equipment entry to the zone. RFID gate for automated vehicle identification, biometric for high-security areas, card reader for personnel access, manual for guard-controlled entry, none for unrestricted areas. Integrates with Port Access Permit system.

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this zone record is currently active in the master data registry. True: active and available for operational use. False: logically deleted or archived. Used for soft-delete pattern and historical record retention without physical deletion.
attributes.references: Data Management Best Practices - Soft Delete Pattern

attributes.name: boundary_coordinates_wkt
attributes.description: Geographic boundary of the zone represented as Well-Known Text (WKT) POLYGON geometry. Enables GIS integration with AVEVA Marine Engineering for port layout visualization, spatial analysis, and automated equipment routing in Terminal Operating Systems.
attributes.references: ISO 19125 Geographic Information - Simple Feature Access

attributes.name: cctv_coverage_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone is monitored by CCTV surveillance system. True: full video surveillance for security and incident investigation. False: no camera coverage. Required for ISPS Level 2+ zones and cargo theft prevention.

attributes.name: centroid_latitude
attributes.description: Latitude coordinate of the zone geometric center in decimal degrees. Used for distance calculations, equipment dispatch optimization, and integration with Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) for cargo location tracking.

attributes.name: centroid_longitude
attributes.description: Longitude coordinate of the zone geometric center in decimal degrees. Used for distance calculations, equipment dispatch optimization, and integration with Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) for cargo location tracking.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the zone was officially opened and entered operational service. Used for asset age calculations, depreciation schedules, and infrastructure lifecycle planning in the source system Maintenance).

attributes.name: customs_controlled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone is under customs authority control as a bonded area or free trade zone. True: customs-controlled area requiring special clearance procedures. False: non-bonded domestic area. Impacts cargo movement restrictions and documentation requirements in Port Community System (PCS).

attributes.name: design_capacity_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Target operational utilization percentage for the zone as designed by port planners. Typically 70-85% to allow operational flexibility. Used as benchmark for KPI reporting and capacity expansion trigger analysis. Expressed as percentage (e.g., 75.00 for 75%).

attributes.name: drainage_system_type
attributes.description: Stormwater management infrastructure type installed in the zone. Storm sewer for direct discharge, retention pond for controlled release, permeable pavement for infiltration, none for natural drainage. Critical for environmental compliance per MARPOL and local water quality regulations tracked in Environmental Monitoring System (EMS).
attributes.references: MARPOL Annex V - Marine Pollution Prevention

attributes.name: environmental_monitoring_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone has installed environmental sensors for air quality, noise, or emissions tracking. True: active monitoring integrated with Environmental Monitoring System (EMS). False: no environmental instrumentation. Required for zones near sensitive receptors or handling bulk materials.

attributes.name: fire_suppression_system
attributes.description: Fire protection infrastructure installed in the zone. Hydrant network for general fire response, foam system for flammable liquid storage, sprinkler for warehouse protection, none for open yard areas. Required for IMDG hazmat zones and insurance compliance.

attributes.name: ground_slot_capacity_teu
attributes.description: Number of Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU) ground slots available for container placement at single-stack height. Represents the base stacking capacity before vertical stacking. Used for yard utilization KPI calculations.

attributes.name: handling_equipment_type
attributes.description: Primary type of cargo handling equipment deployed in this zone. RTG (Rubber Tyred Gantry) for automated container yards, ASC (Automated Stacking Crane) for rail-mounted operations, reach stacker for flexible container handling, forklift for warehouse operations, mobile crane for heavy lift, none for passive storage areas. Determines operational capacity and throughput rates.

attributes.name: hazmat_approved_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone is certified and equipped for storage and handling of dangerous goods per International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. True: approved for IMDG cargo with appropriate safety infrastructure. False: non-hazmat zone. Drives cargo acceptance rules in Terminal Operating System.
attributes.references: IMDG Code - International Maritime Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: isps_facility_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.isps_facility_record. PFSO tracks zone-specific security levels, access restrictions, and PFSP co

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal infrastructure inspection for safety, structural integrity, and regulatory compliance. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling in Maximo Asset Management and Port State Control (PSC) readiness.

attributes.name: last_resurfacing_date
attributes.description: Date when the zone pavement was last resurfaced or rehabilitated. Used to calculate pavement age, predict maintenance cycles, and schedule preventive maintenance in Maximo Asset Management system.

attributes.name: lease_status
attributes.description: Commercial arrangement governing zone usage rights. Port operated: directly managed by port authority. Leased terminal operator: long-term concession to terminal operator. Leased cargo owner: dedicated to specific shipper/consignee. Subleased: operator has subleased to third party. Vacant: available for lease. Drives revenue recognition and billing in the source system

attributes.name: lighting_type
attributes.description: Type of illumination infrastructure installed in the zone for 24/7 operations. LED high mast for energy-efficient area lighting, halogen flood for legacy installations, none for daylight-only operations. Impacts operational hours, safety compliance, and energy consumption tracking in Environmental Management System (EMS).

attributes.name: maximum_stack_height
attributes.description: Maximum number of container tiers (vertical stacking levels) permitted in this zone based on pavement strength, equipment Safe Working Load (SWL), and operational safety requirements. Typically ranges from 3-6 tiers for yard operations.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory infrastructure inspection. Calculated based on regulatory requirements, pavement condition, and operational intensity. Triggers work order generation in Maximo for inspection planning.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the zone. Operational: actively in use for cargo handling. Maintenance: temporarily unavailable for scheduled or emergency maintenance. Closed: administratively closed but not decommissioned. Planned: approved for construction but not yet operational. Decommissioned: permanently removed from service.

attributes.name: paved_area_sqm
attributes.description: Surface area with hard pavement (concrete or asphalt) suitable for heavy equipment operations and container stacking in square meters (m²). Critical for determining operational capacity and maintenance planning.

attributes.name: pavement_condition_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of pavement structural integrity and surface condition. Excellent: no defects, full load capacity. Good: minor wear, full operational capacity. Fair: moderate deterioration, reduced heavy equipment operations. Poor: significant cracking/rutting, maintenance required. Critical: structural failure risk, immediate repair needed. Drives CAPEX maintenance planning.

attributes.name: rail_access_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone has direct rail track access for intermodal rail operations. True: rail-connected for on-dock rail loading/unloading. False: truck-only access. Critical for intermodal logistics planning and rail operator coordination.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this terminal zone record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and regulatory compliance reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: record_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated or last updated this zone record. NAVIS N4 for TOS-managed zones, AVEVA Marine for engineering-designed zones, manual entry for ad-hoc additions, GIS import for spatial data loads, legacy migration for historical data conversion. Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Data Governance Framework - System of Record Standards

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this terminal zone record was last modified. Tracks data currency for change data capture, synchronization with operational systems (NAVIS N4, AVEVA), and audit compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: reefer_plug_count
attributes.description: Number of electrical connection points (reefer plugs) available for refrigerated container (reefer) power supply. Critical for cold chain cargo capacity planning and reefer slot allocation in Terminal Operating System.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special handling instructions, temporary restrictions, or historical context not captured in structured fields. Used by terminal planners and operations managers for knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: security_level
attributes.description: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code security level assigned to the zone. Level 1: normal operations with minimum security measures. Level 2: heightened risk requiring additional security. Level 3: imminent threat requiring maximum protective measures. Drives access control and surveillance requirements.
attributes.references: ISPS Code - International Ship and Port Facility Security

attributes.name: total_area_sqm
attributes.description: Total surface area of the zone in square meters (m²). Includes paved, unpaved, and built-up areas. Used for capacity planning, lease calculations, and infrastructure investment analysis.

attributes.name: total_capacity_teu
attributes.description: Maximum theoretical container capacity in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEU) when stacked to maximum allowable height. Calculated as ground_slot_capacity_teu × maximum_stack_height. Used for strategic capacity planning and terminal expansion analysis.

attributes.name: truck_access_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone has direct road access for truck operations. True: truck-accessible for drayage and delivery operations. False: restricted access requiring internal transfer. Impacts gate operations and dwell time calculations.

attributes.name: vessel_side_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone is located directly adjacent to berth/quay for ship-to-shore operations. True: vessel-side zone for direct discharge/loading operations. False: landside zone requiring horizontal transport. Affects Ship-to-Shore (STS) crane reach and vessel operation efficiency.

attributes.name: weighbridge_available_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the zone has an integrated weighbridge (truck scale) for container/cargo weight verification. True: weighbridge installed for SOLAS VGM (Verified Gross Mass) compliance. False: no weighing capability. Mandatory for container export zones per SOLAS Amendment.

products.name: infrastructure_berth_reservation
products.description: This association product represents the reservation/assignment event between a berth and a vessel call booking. It captures the operational allocation of a specific berth to a specific vessel call, including reservation priority, tidal constraints, planned and actual berthing/departure times, berth side assignment, and utilization metrics. Each record links one berth to one vessel call booking with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific berthing operation.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, a berth can host many vessel calls over time (sequential reservations), and a vessel call can legitimately require multiple berths during a single port visit. Multi-berth operations occur for large cruise ships, ro-ro vessels with multiple loading points, or when a vessel shifts berths mid-call due to cargo operations or berth availability. The berth reservation is a recognized operational entity that port operations teams actively manage, with its own lifecycle, priority levels, and timing attributes distinct from both the berth infrastructure and the booking request.

products.name: infrastructure_anchorage_booking
products.description: This association product represents the operational booking and assignment of a vessel call to a specific anchorage area within the port. It captures the anchorage-specific coordination data that exists only in the context of linking a vessel call booking to an anchorage area, including the reason for anchorage use, requested and actual anchor drop times, duration, priority level, and VTS coordination reference. Each record represents one anchorage assignment within a vessel's port call lifecycle.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, a vessel call booking can require multiple anchorage assignments during a single port visit (e.g., quarantine anchorage upon arrival, waiting anchorage before berth availability, bunkering anchorage for refueling). Conversely, an anchorage area hosts many different vessel calls over time. The anchorage booking is an operational coordination entity actively managed by VTS and port operations, tracking reason codes, requested/actual anchor drop times, duration, priority, and VTS coordination for each vessel-anchorage assignment.

products.name: infrastructure_berth_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the contractual allocation of berths to commercial agreement holders (shipping lines, stevedoring companies, terminal operators, concessionaires). It captures the business arrangement whereby specific berths are licensed, leased, or allocated under commercial agreements with defined time windows, priority levels, exclusivity terms, and performance commitments. Each record links one berth to one agreement with attributes that exist only in the context of this allocation relationship, enabling time-sliced berth sharing, priority-based allocation, and multi-berth concessions.. Existence Justification: In maritime port operations, berths are allocated to commercial parties (shipping lines, stevedoring companies, terminal operators) under various agreement types including concessions, stevedoring contracts, and service agreements. A single berth can be shared by multiple operators through time-sliced allocation (e.g., weekday vs weekend use), priority-based allocation (exclusive vs shared access), or seasonal allocation (cruise season vs cargo season). Conversely, a single multi-terminal concession agreement or stevedoring contract routinely covers multiple berths across different quays or terminals. The allocation itself is an actively managed business entity with specific attributes: allocation time windows, priority levels, exclusivity terms, berth-specific throughput commitments, and berth-specific revenue share percentages.

products.name: project_permit
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory permit application and compliance relationship between infrastructure projects and the permits required to execute them. In maritime port infrastructure development, large CAPEX projects require portfolios of permits from multiple regulatory authorities (environmental, marine, construction, safety), and conversely, master permits (e.g., port development zone permits) can authorize multiple related projects. Each record links one infrastructure project to one infrastructure permit and captures application-specific data including submission dates, approval dates, project-specific compliance status, cost allocation for permit acquisition, and the responsible project officer managing that permit relationship. This is actively managed by project compliance teams through permit registers and regulatory tracking systems.. Existence Justification: In maritime port infrastructure development, large CAPEX projects routinely require portfolios of multiple permits from different regulatory authorities (environmental impact assessments, construction permits, dredging permits, marine discharge permits, heritage approvals). Conversely, master permits such as port development zone permits or environmental framework permits can authorize multiple related infrastructure projects within their scope. Project compliance teams actively manage these relationships through permit registers, tracking application dates, approval status, compliance obligations, and cost allocation for each project-permit combination.
